_notes: Her window is dark, and her window is never dark. Two ways home, the empty hall, and the climb in through the workroom window.
Scenes 18-25 of the prologue as it was before the split; `--scene story:<index>` still counts across the whole prologue, not within this file.

lines: Her window is ahead now.
The shutters are closed.
Old green shutters that fold back against the brick, and they have been folded back every evening of my life: in rain, in frost, in the week the chimney caught.
She did not close them for weather. She did not close them for company. She did not close them.
Something in me tried to file that and could not find the drawer. So I did what anybody does with a fact that will not sit down. I told myself she was out.
Two ways home from here.
The long way passes the Lamplighters' hall — whatever silenced the lamps went wrong there first. Eleven minutes, perhaps twelve.
The fast way is over the fences, and the fences are a young cat's road.
choices: The long way — see what silenced the lamps
scenes.art_desc: Deep in the fogged lane at night, every street lamp dark, one lamplighter's ladder still leaning against an unlit lamp
Lamplighters' guild hall interior, abandoned mid-shift: racked ladders, cold kettle, one silver thread glinting on a lamp-hook
lines: I took the long way, and I have had a long time to decide why. Because the route had a wrongness at the head of it. Because her voice said look before you leap, Ash. Because the fences would have cost me a breath I had already had taken off me once tonight.
All three are true. I have not decided.
The hall stood open. Door wide, ladders racked, coats on their pegs. The kettle on the little stove was cold, and a guild hall's kettle is never cold.
Forty men and women walk out of this room every evening and light a city. Nobody was in it.
Caught on a lamp-hook by the door, glinting where it had snagged: a thread of silver. HER stitching. I would know it under floodwater. Why was she HERE?
notes: ❋ Her Stitching joins your deck — a Moonlight 2, and the only card of its kind you own.

lines: Out of the hall and eleven streets home, and I do not remember eight of them.
The fog thinning near the Mere. Ordinary houses, ordinary gates, a cat crossing an ordinary city at a speed that was going to cost him.
Her street. Her gate. Her drainpipe, the one I have used nine hundred times, and up — slower than nine hundred times, my back legs arguing the whole way.

scenes.art_desc: Ash in full sprint leaping between fence tops at night, fog blurred with speed, a dark window ahead
lines: Over the fences, which are a young cat's road, and I pay for every one of them.
The Lamplighters' hall goes by dark on my left. Later. If there is a later.
Under the gate, up the drainpipe I have used nine hundred times, and in. Fast enough that something inside is still busy.
In through the workroom window. A door has never once been an obstacle. It is, however, always an insult.
The house is doing the wrong thing with sound. A kettle screaming and nobody going to it.
The workroom first, and the workroom is wrong. The threads on the walls, forty years of her work hung like a garden, cut.
Every one of them snipped at the same height, cleanly, as if by someone tidying.
The parlor door stands open, and I do not go through it. Not yet. I stop at the threshold, low, and I look.

scenes.art_desc: The Unpicked: a person-shaped absence woven from the room's own unravelled threads, standing in a doorway
lines: Something is standing in the parlor doorway, wearing the room.
It is person-shaped the way a coat on a hook is person-shaped, and it is made of her threads — it has been pulling them out of the walls and putting them ON.
It is still working. It does not stop when it sees me. That is the part I will keep: it looked at me, decided I was not an interruption, and went back to it.
Every hair I have is standing up. Good. Let them.
